reference.title: Resistance Band Seated Biceps Curl
reference.listing: Animated GIF (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (the proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the movement follows the name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, short squeeze, about 2.4 s down

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen; the band is hardest at the top of the curl, where it is stretched most
prescription.progression: Band tension is user-chosen: pick a band you can curl for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion); add reps, then a stronger band or a shorter grip on the band.

cues.text: Sit tall on the end of a bench, feet flat about hip width and well out in front, the middle of the band under the feet; hold an end in each hand, arms straight beside the bench, palms forward.
Breathe out and curl both hands up, elbows by your sides.
Squeeze at the top, where the band is tightest; wrists straight, shoulders down.
Breathe in and lower slowly against the band to straight arms.
Sit tall, a little tension left in the band; repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Rocking the trunk back to stretch the band
mistakes.fix: Sit tall and still; use a lighter band.
Keep the elbows by the sides; only the forearms move.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band snap the hands down
mistakes.fix: Take 2-3 s to lower all the way to straight arms.
Sit up on the sit bones, chest up.

kinematics.norm: Full range: mean elbow range was about 117-123 degrees across barbell, EZ-bar and alternating dumbbell curls (Marcolin 2018)

kinematics.measure: Forearm rotation (wrist pron channel, 0 = palm up/forward, 90 = thumb up)
kinematics.norm: The supinated grip gave the highest biceps activity in the lifting phase; neutral grips shift work toward the brachioradialis (Coratella 2023)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm from the trunk line (sagittal)
kinematics.norm: Elbows stay near the sides; a small forward drift at the top is normal, a big swing shifts work to the front deltoid (clinical opinion)

Elastic tension rises as the band stretches, so the load is highest where the band is longest; at matched effort, elastic tubing and dumbbells gave similar muscle activity in upper-body exercises (Andersen 2010); with the band under the feet in front, the load rises toward the top of the curl
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion); biceps activity was lower while lowering than lifting at the same load (Oliveira 2009)

Coratella et al. 2023, biceps brachii and brachioradialis excitation in biceps curl exercise: different handgrips, different synergy (Sports 11(3):64; PMC10054060)

Augustin, Pinero, Enes, Mohan, Sapuppo, Coleman, Wolf, Korakakis, Swinton, Nippard and Schoenfeld 2025, do cheaters prosper? Externally supplied momentum in curls and pushdowns and upper-arm hypertrophy (Int J Exerc Sci 18(3):329-342)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjornlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Elbow or shoulder pain: use a lighter band and shorten the range; stop if pain is sharp (clinical opinion).
Check the band for nicks or tears before each set and make sure it cannot slip off its anchor (under the feet, round the upright). Keep both feet firmly on the band so it cannot slip out and snap up.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Wrist or elbow pain with the palms up: turn to a neutral (hammer) grip.
Too hard at the top: move the feet closer to the bench to slacken the band.
progressions: Stronger band, or the feet further forward.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Main elbow flexor and forearm supinator; with a supinated grip it worked harder than with neutral (+12%) or pronated (+19%) grips in the lifting phase (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Main elbow flexor and forearm supinator; with a supinated grip it worked harder than with neutral (+12%) or pronated (+19%) grips in the lifting phase (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Brachioradialis (mapped to the forearm extensor region) assists elbow flexion, most with the forearm near neutral.
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_l: Brachioradialis (mapped to the forearm extensor region) assists elbow flexion, most with the forearm near neutral.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Wrist and finger flexors hold the band and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Wrist and finger flexors hold the band and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Steadies the shoulder so the upper arm stays put; it rises if the elbow drifts forward.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Steadies the shoulder so the upper arm stays put; it rises if the elbow drifts forward.
muscleNotes.core: Holds the unsupported trunk tall; sitting takes the legs and hips out so the weight cannot be swung up.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the back tall without a backrest.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the back tall without a backrest.
